semantic_correction.stem: A client is starting metformin hydrochloride extended-release tablets for type 2 diabetes. Which teaching should the nurse include?

options.A: Take the tablet with the evening meal, swallow it whole, and follow gradual dose increases made according to glycemic control and tolerability.
options.B: Take the tablet with the evening meal, split it if swallowing is difficult, and increase the dose the next day if glucose remains above the target range.
options.C: Take the tablet whole before breakfast on an empty stomach, and expect dose increases every day or two until the glucose goal is reached.
options.D: Take the tablet with the evening meal, chew it thoroughly for better absorption, and keep the starting dose unchanged despite later prescriber adjustments.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current U.S. metformin extended-release labeling directs patients to swallow the extended-release tablets whole and not crush, cut, or chew them. The labeled starting regimen is once daily with the evening meal, and dose increases are made in 500-mg weekly increments based on glycemic control and tolerability. Therefore A is correct. B includes the correct meal timing but incorrectly permits splitting and next-day self-escalation. C uses the wrong meal timing and an excessively rapid titration schedule. D includes the evening meal but incorrectly advises chewing the extended-release tablet and disregarding later prescribed dose adjustments.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach clients starting metformin extended-release to take the medication with the evening meal, swallow the tablet whole, and follow gradual prescribed titration based on glycemic response and tolerability.
semantic_correction.source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine DailyMed / U.S. Food and Drug Administration labeling

semantic_correction.source_locator: Section 2.1 Adult Dosage and Administration / Highlights: swallow metformin hydrochloride extended-release tablets whole and never crush, cut, or chew; starting dose 500 mg once daily with the evening meal; increase the dose in increments of 500 mg weekly based on glycemic control and tolerability, up to the labeled maximum.
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: Metformin extended-release is swallowed whole, taken with the evening meal, and titrated gradually in 500-mg weekly increments based on glycemic control and tolerability.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup retained the metformin-ER teaching construct, removed the original absolute-word distractor cue, balanced option length, and anchored the key to the June 2026 label's evening-meal, whole-tablet, and weekly-titration instructions.

scope_exclusions.renal_function: The item does not test eGFR thresholds, renal contraindications, or initiation restrictions.
scope_exclusions.lactic_acidosis: The current boxed warning and April 2026 label change are acknowledged by currentness review but are not part of this administration-teaching construct.
scope_exclusions.contrast: Iodinated-contrast interruption rules are not tested.
scope_exclusions.maximum_dose: No maximum daily dose is required to answer the item.
scope_exclusions.self_titration: The key describes prescribed gradual titration; it does not authorize the client to change the dose independently.
scope_exclusions.immediate_release: The item is specific to the extended-release formulation and does not generalize the administration schedule to immediate-release metformin.

near_duplicate_check.note: Targeted GitHub search for ‘metformin extended release evening meal swallow whole 500 mg weekly’ returned no indexed repository match. No broad bank scan was performed.

option_audit.A: Correct. It accurately combines the three labeled teaching points while preserving clinician-directed titration.
option_audit.B: Plausible because the evening-meal timing is correct, but extended-release tablets should not be split and dose escalation is not a next-day client decision.
option_audit.C: Plausible because some medications are taken fasting and diabetes therapy is titrated, but both the meal timing and titration interval are incorrect.
option_audit.D: Plausible because the evening meal is correct, but chewing is incompatible with the extended-release instructions and later prescribed adjustments should be followed.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. A alone has correct meal timing, formulation handling, and gradual titration. Each distractor contains a material administration or titration error.

cueing_check.note: The key is not longest; all four are parallel multi-part teaching statements and no only/always/never/every cue is used.

blueprint_audit.entry_level_relevance: Medication administration and client medication education are explicit 2026 NCLEX-RN activities, and recognizing formulation-specific administration is a core entry-level medication-safety task.
blueprint_audit.visual_verification: VERIFIED. Official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan screenshot pageno 15 / printed p.12 was successfully retrieved August 20, 2026 and visibly shows the cited Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies activity statements.

source_verification.note: The live DailyMed label was rechecked August 20, 2026. It was updated June 10, 2026 / revised June 2026 and directly supports whole-tablet administration, the evening meal, and 500-mg weekly titration.
